sections.text: When I see Thy mouths with their fearful jaws like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation, I lose all sense of place; I find no rest. Be merciful, O Lord in whom this universe abides!
All these sons of Dhritarashtra, with the hosts of princes, Bheeshma, Drona and Karna, as well as the other warrior chiefs belonging to our side;
I see them all rushing headlong into Thy mouths, with terrible tusks, horrible to behold. Some are mangled between thy jaws, with their heads crushed to atoms.

So we had been discussing chapter 11, Vishwarupadarshan yoga, the Cosmic Form. We all want to know Bhagavan. But Bhagavan says, if I show you my Roop, it may not be as pleasant as you think.
So Arjuna asked for it and he got what he wished for. Both concepts of space and time are wiped out from his mind. Now he sees this entire Jagat without any space, and also without any time difference.
So first he described what he saw and said, I see that everything is within you. I see with many mouths, many hands, many stomachs, many legs. In other words, all the legs and all the mouths which I consider to be individually assigned to individual are all yours.
I see them all into you. He also saw everything that he has ever encountered in his life. Devas, all the deities -- I see all of them in you.
So he described what he sees. Then he also sees the condition of other beings looking at this great form: all these people are entering into you. Some are fearful and some are praising your glory.
Those who have not comprehended the reality are fearful of it. When we are not sure about the outcome of our actions in life, we are fearful. Those who are wise enough to not get perturbed by whatever the outcome is, they are blissful and praising the Lord because they have accepted everything.
So I see those wise people are praising you, but others are entering into you in fear. And then he says, I also see you as Vishnu. I see you as that Almighty Vishnu.
Kiritinam Gadinam, Chakri Namcha. With all your attributes, I see you. But then he says, I also dont see any middle, end or beginning.
And all the space between the heavens and earth is filled with you alone. Up till now what I considered nothingness -- there is no such thing as nothingness anymore. Everything is you and you alone.
So I see you all around me and everything in you. And now I also see how the world is looking at you, how the other beings react. He still keeps himself out of this.
He is an observer observing an object. His experience is all objective. Right now he is describing whats happening to others.
This is how we observe our world. We keep ourselves out of it and then say, oh, he is not doing exercise, he is going to be suffering, he is smoking, he is going to have cancer. We keep ourselves out of it.
We look at the world and see how they are doing and how they are feeling and how they are behaving. So up to now he is looking at everything and saying, everybody is entering into you. Some are fearful, some are praising you.
I see the deities, I see everything into. You are filling all the spaces. But then he starts having the other side of the experience.
Its not all wonderful -- life has its positive moments and negative moments. And when you focus on one, you can always give a biography of a person showing how great he was and how accomplished he was. Every funeral I go to, I realize there is not an average person in this world.
Everyone says how great the person was, what he accomplished, and how loving he was. I have never heard somebody say, He was such an average person. He didnt really accomplish much in his life.
He was a terrible husband, a cruel father. Because we focus on what is good in that person, we highlight all the goodness in him. So up till now Arjuna was only focusing on the divinity. Then he sees Brahma seated on the lotus.
All the deities are praising, all the vasavas and maruts and everybody is praising. And they are all dumbfounded just looking at this great. Theyre looking in wonderment.
Even the wise person also gets awed by the nature. Even people like Einstein, who are pure scientists -- he could not figure out what Gods game is all about. Thats why he said, God doesnt play dice. He had complete faith that God wouldnt be doing something random.
He had faith in Gods laws of nature, that we can figure them out. This world is very predictable from our perspective; theres nothing unpredictable in this world, really. With that predictability, we can plan our life.
Ill get up at 6 oclock and then Ill do this, then Ill be at class at 10. We can plan that because its predictable. Everything you can predict from when I leave my house.
The unpredictable part is what will happen during that period. And once we look at that, we start getting fearful. Well, you can get in an accident.
You are at Times Square walking around and somebody just drives a car onto the sidewalk. Its unthinkable, unpredictable. Unpredictable things do occur.
So there is positive and there is negative. From our perspective, from our relative world, there is positive and negative. Now Arjuna, from his perspective, says what is also not so pleasant.
He says: Nabhas Sprisham Diptam Anek Varnam Vyattananam Dipta Vishala Netram Drashtva Hi Tvam Pravyathitantaratma Dhritim Na Vindami Shamam Cha Vishno. Having seen your form touching the sky, inflaming with many colors, your open mouth and fiery eyes -- I am shaken up inside. I have no courage, no peace.
Up till now, I had a place in this world where I had staked myself and said, This is where I am, and this is who I am in relationship to the world. The moment I feel insignificant anywhere -- in my organization, in my society, in my community, in my family -- I start getting depressed. We keep our balance by having that self-assessment of ourselves as an important being. The moment we drop that, we become completely fearful.
We do not know where we stand. Thats why when people retire, they often lose their sense of what is important. Roger Ailes ruled Fox channel for a long time.
As soon as he was disgraced and ousted, he died within a year. Had he still been at Fox, he probably would have continued for another 10 years. People lose their bearings in life and therefore lose their stability.
So he said, Dhritim Na Vindami Shamam Cha Vishno -- I do not see what I can do. I dont think Im capable of anything, and I have no peace because of that. Danshtra Karalani Cha Te Mukhani -- now he gives the other side of the coin.
Up till now, he was talking about all existence, seeing everything existing in you. I see that everything is existing in you and everything is supported by you. But now he says Danshtra Karalani Cha Te Mukhani Drashtva Eva Kala Anala Sannibhani -- I see in your mouth these terrible teeth, fearsome teeth, and fire blazing in your mouth.
Disho Na Jane -- I dont see the directions. I do not see my place in life; I do not see my place in this universe. Up till now, I had a complete sense of who I am and where I am.
In my family, there is a placement -- I know who I am. I know who I am in my community. I know who I am in my company.
I know who I am as a citizen. There is a bearing I can describe. Im at 1537B Knuckles Road.
I can tell you how to come to me. There is a complete sense of placement and direction. I am such-and-such in the community.
So I had a complete sense of my worth and my place in this universe. But once I see the mortality -- that everything is rushing towards you, and so am I -- that changes everything. Right now, I see my life in a static picture.
I always see myself as existing now. Its a static picture in my head. Everybody else sees me getting old.
Its very hard for you to imagine yourself to be growing and deteriorating. You have to constantly remind yourself, you know, I cant do that anymore. I have to keep telling myself, Im an old man.
Because I dont see myself as an old man. I have to remind myself. The other day I was reading something.
Some psychoanalyst says that the difference between a normal person and a psychopath is that a psychopath has to be reminded that certain behavior is not acceptable. A normal person naturally knows what is acceptable behavior in a society. A person suffering from that mental condition who becomes a sociopath or psychopath does not have that natural bearing.
Somebody has to constantly tell him, This is not acceptable, this is not acceptable. Only then can he function in society. So Arjuna said, having seen this mortality -- that everything is rushing towards you, that there are terrible teeth and blazing fire in your mouth, that you are the resting place of everything, that all names and forms, including mine, will be destroyed in you -- therefore, I do not know what my place in life is. I am fast-forwarding my life right now.
Normally, I see my life one frame at a time. Therefore, it is a static picture I am seeing. I see every moment as one frame at a time.
I have forgotten the last frame, and I dont know the next frame. Its a static picture, and I consider that as my existence. But fast-forward my life.
We have DVR, obviously -- we record all the shows. Sometimes I say, Meena, you have 24 episodes of this Satyameva Jayate. When are we going to get rid of them? She says, Oh, no, no, Ill finish.
Ill do speed watching. I had heard of speed reading, but speed watching! Fast-forward for three minutes and the whole show is done. A persons whole episode is over in two minutes. If our life is fast-forwarded, the eulogy at the end of your life tells the story.
Somebody will give your entire life in two minutes: he was born in Surat, went to high school here, then went to architecture school, went to Africa, then taught Bhagavad Gita, and died. Entire life summarized in two minutes or less. When you fast-forward your life, the only thing you see is that you are rushing towards your death.
Thats all youre doing every moment. And we have to keep reminding ourselves -- we have birthday celebrations to say, This is not bad so far. So he said, I do not know where I stand. Disho Na Jane Na Labhe Cha Sharma.
Having seen my mortality and insignificance, I cant find any peace. What is the purpose of my life? We completely realize that all I consider to be my abilities are of no value when you are sick. And I have explained this before -- when you are sick, you can tell me anything about anything, but Im not listening right now.
I just cant feel good about anything. I have a fever of 105 and you want to talk to me about Bhagavad Gita? Forget about it right now. I cant find any bearing.
And Arjuna said, Im in that situation. I cant find it. So he said, Prasida Devesha Jagannivasa -- be gracious to me, O Lord of the universe.
This is, the true surrender. Intellectually saying Bhagavan, tera tujhko arpan, kya lage mera -- intellectual surrender really means nothing, because you still think I am surrendering. That ego is still very much there. I am good, I am doing puja, I am doing meditation. That I is so solidly there that the surrender is of not much value.

Arjuna now sees the fearsome mouths with terrible jaws like glowing fires at the dissolution of creation and cries out: I lose all sense of place; I find no rest. Even more disturbing, he sees all the sons of Dhritarashtra, Bhishma, Drona, Karna, and warriors from both armies rushing headlong into these terrible mouths, some mangled between Thy jaws, with their heads crushed to atoms. The cosmic vision has revealed not just abstract unity but the concrete reality that everyone Arjuna knows is heading toward destruction. This is the point where intellectual understanding becomes visceral. We all know that everyone dies, but Arjuna is seeing it happen - not as a future event but as a present reality from the cosmic perspective. The verse about losing all sense of place is particularly significant. Our sense of identity depends on knowing our place - in family, society, time. When we see that this placement is temporary and that we are all rushing toward the same dissolution, our ordinary bearings disappear. This is terrifying for the ego but liberating for the seeker who is ready. For todays practice, try s exercise of fast-forwarding your life. Imagine someone giving your eulogy - your entire life summarized in two minutes. What remains significant from this perspective? What falls away as trivial? Then extend this to everyone you will interact with today: each person you see is also moving toward their end. This is not meant to be morbid but to shift priorities. What conflicts would dissolve if you truly saw the temporary nature of all positions and identities? What kindness would become more natural? Let the awareness of universal mortality open compassion rather than despair.
